newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks fall on Dow, U.S. interest rate fear.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks fall on Dow, U.S. interest rate fear.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed off session lows on Monday, but were still down sharply as Wall Street stocks sold off on fears of further rises in U.S. interest rates.

"The bourse has broken support now. An important factor for us which is hitting the markets is a change in outlook for U.S. interest rates," said Jaime Fernandez, an equity analyst at the Interacciones brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended down 94.96 points, or 2.47 percent, at 3,747.98.
"Dealers are moving ahead of expected additional hikes (in U.S. interest rates). We expect another increase in May, and a total rise of 50-100 basis points for the year as a whole," Fernandez added.
"Volume was low because many are still on vacation. Furthermore, there's no news, neither good nor bad," he said.
Trading volume was a lifeless 48.9 million shares. Traders said this was due to caution while awaiting further developments on Wall Street.
"Until the slump on Wall Street is over, how do you tell what price to buy at?" a Mexico City floor trader said.

Money market traders forecast gains of up to 60 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Tuesday evening's central bank auction of government securities. Banco de Mexico assigned primary 28-day Cetes at 20.59 percent last week. On
the broad market, 112 stocks changed hands, of which decliners trounced gainers by 80 to 13.
Telecoms firm Telmex L class, which ended off 44 centavos at 15.22 pesos, accounted for 17 percent of all shares tradedand weighed most heavily on the market.
Telmex ADRs meanwhile ended down 1/2 at 38-1/2 on Wall Street.
"Telmex is down, but fighting back," a floor trader said. "The market feels they are doing better than expected in the long distance market.
Telmex saw its decades old monopoly of long distance calls end on January 1 in some state capitals. Mexico City residents will shortly be balloted on their preferred long distance carriers.
Retail chain Sears gained 60 centavos to 13.50 pesos.
